banana_cordana.fertilizer_quantity: 200 g per plant, applied every 2 months
banana_cordana.pesticide_quantity: 2.5 g per litre of water; spray every 10–14 days
banana_cordana.description: Cordana leaf spot is a fungal disease. Remove affected leaves, improve field sanitation, and apply a recommended fungicide to control spread.

banana_healthy.pesticide: No pesticide required — preventive neem oil only
banana_healthy.pesticide_quantity: 5 ml neem oil per litre of water, monthly
banana_healthy.description: Banana plant is healthy. Continue balanced fertilization, regular irrigation, and routine field monitoring to maintain plant health.

banana_pestalotiopsis.pesticide_quantity: 3 g per litre of water; spray every 10 days
banana_pestalotiopsis.description: Pestalotiopsis causes necrotic leaf spots. Remove infected leaves, avoid overhead irrigation, and apply copper-based fungicide at first sign.

banana_sigatoka.pesticide_quantity: 1 ml propiconazole per litre, every 14 days
banana_sigatoka.description: Sigatoka is a serious fungal leaf disease. Use resistant varieties, prune infected leaves, and follow a regular fungicide spray schedule.

corn_common_rust.fertilizer_quantity: 120 kg N per hectare, split in 2 doses
corn_common_rust.pesticide_quantity: 2.5 g mancozeb per litre, every 10–14 days
corn_common_rust.description: Common rust produces reddish-brown pustules on leaves. Use resistant hybrids, balanced nitrogen, and foliar fungicide if infection is severe.

corn_gray_leaf_spot.fertilizer_quantity: 100 kg N, 60 kg P2O5, 80 kg K2O per hectare
corn_gray_leaf_spot.pesticide_quantity: 1 ml per litre of water, every 14 days
corn_gray_leaf_spot.description: Gray leaf spot is favoured by continuous corn. Rotate crops, bury residue, and apply foliar fungicide at tasseling if disease pressure is high.

corn_healthy.fertilizer_quantity: 120 kg N, 60 kg P2O5, 40 kg K2O per hectare
corn_healthy.pesticide: No pesticide required — preventive care only
corn_healthy.description: Corn crop is healthy. Maintain balanced nutrition, weed control, and monitor regularly for any early signs of disease or pest attack.

corn_northern_leaf_blight.fertilizer_quantity: 150 kg N per hectare in split applications
corn_northern_leaf_blight.pesticide_quantity: 2.5 g mancozeb per litre, every 10–14 days
corn_northern_leaf_blight.description: Northern leaf blight causes long cigar-shaped lesions. Use resistant hybrids, crop rotation, and timely fungicide sprays at early disease onset.

cotton_bacterial_blight.fertilizer: NPK 19-19-19 with potassium for disease resistance
cotton_bacterial_blight.fertilizer_quantity: 100 kg N, 50 kg P2O5, 50 kg K2O per hectare
cotton_bacterial_blight.pesticide_quantity: 3 g copper + 0.5 g streptocycline per 10 litres water
cotton_bacterial_blight.description: Bacterial blight is seed-borne. Use disease-free certified seed, treat seed with hot water, and spray copper-based bactericide at first symptoms.

cotton_cotton_leaf_curl.fertilizer_quantity: 120 kg N, 60 kg P2O5, 60 kg K2O per hectare
cotton_cotton_leaf_curl.pesticide_quantity: 0.5 ml per litre for sucking pest vector control
cotton_cotton_leaf_curl.description: Cotton leaf curl virus is transmitted by whitefly. Control vector with imidacloprid, remove infected plants, and use virus-resistant varieties.

cotton_fusarium_wilt.fertilizer_quantity: 90 kg N, 60 kg P2O5, 60 kg K2O per hectare
cotton_fusarium_wilt.pesticide_quantity: 1 g carbendazim per litre, drench at root zone
cotton_fusarium_wilt.description: Fusarium wilt is a soil-borne fungus. Use resistant varieties, treat seed with carbendazim, and practice long crop rotation with non-host crops.

cotton_healthy.fertilizer_quantity: 120 kg N, 60 kg P2O5, 60 kg K2O per hectare
cotton_healthy.pesticide: No pesticide required — preventive IPM only
cotton_healthy.description: Cotton crop is healthy. Continue balanced fertilization, regular pest scouting, and follow IPM practices to keep the crop in good condition.

grape_black_measles.fertilizer_quantity: 500 g per vine in 2 split doses
grape_black_measles.description: Black measles affects canes and fruit. Prune infected wood, destroy debris, and apply protectant fungicide during the early growing season.

grape_black_rot.fertilizer_quantity: 400 g per vine, split in 2 applications
grape_black_rot.pesticide_quantity: 2 g myclobutanil per litre, every 14 days
grape_black_rot.description: Black rot damages grapes and leaves. Remove mummified fruit, prune for airflow, and apply fungicide at 7–14 day intervals during humid weather.

grape_healthy.pesticide: No pesticide required — preventive neem oil only
grape_healthy.pesticide_quantity: 5 ml neem oil per litre, monthly
grape_healthy.description: Grapevine is healthy. Continue regular pruning, balanced nutrition, and monitor for early signs of fungal disease, especially in humid weather.

grape_isariopsis_leaf_spot.description: Isariopsis leaf spot causes angular brown lesions. Improve canopy airflow, remove infected leaves, and apply carbendazim at recommended intervals.

mango_anthracnose.fertilizer_quantity: 1–2 kg per tree per year, split in 2 doses
mango_anthracnose.pesticide_quantity: 1 g carbendazim per litre, every 14 days
mango_anthracnose.description: Anthracnose causes black spots on leaves and fruit. Prune dead twigs, harvest carefully, and apply fungicide during flowering and fruit development.

mango_bacterial_canker.pesticide_quantity: 3 g copper + 0.5 g streptocycline per 10 litres
mango_bacterial_canker.description: Bacterial canker affects leaves and twigs. Use disease-free planting material, avoid wounding, and apply copper-based bactericide during monsoon.

mango_healthy.pesticide: No pesticide required — preventive neem oil only
mango_healthy.pesticide_quantity: 5 ml neem oil per litre, monthly
mango_healthy.description: Mango tree is healthy. Continue regular manuring, mulching, and routine inspection for any pest or disease symptoms on leaves and fruit.

mango_powdery_mildew.pesticide_quantity: 3 g sulphur per litre, every 10 days during flowering
mango_powdery_mildew.description: Powdery mildew affects inflorescences and young fruit. Spray sulphur at panicle emergence and repeat at 10-day intervals during flowering.

paddy_bacterial_leaf_blight.fertilizer: NPK 20-10-10 with reduced nitrogen at tillering
paddy_bacterial_leaf_blight.fertilizer_quantity: 100 kg N, 50 kg P2O5, 50 kg K2O per hectare
paddy_bacterial_leaf_blight.pesticide_quantity: 2 g copper + 0.5 g streptocycline per 10 litres water
paddy_bacterial_leaf_blight.description: Bacterial leaf blight spreads in flooded, humid fields. Drain excess water, avoid excess nitrogen, and apply copper-based bactericide at first sign.

paddy_brown_spot.fertilizer_quantity: 120 kg N, 60 kg P2O5, 60 kg K2O per hectare
paddy_brown_spot.pesticide_quantity: 2.5 g mancozeb per litre, every 10–14 days
paddy_brown_spot.description: Brown spot is associated with nutrient deficiency. Apply balanced NPK with potash, treat seed with carbendazim, and foliar spray mancozeb if needed.

paddy_healthy.fertilizer_quantity: 120 kg N, 60 kg P2O5, 40 kg K2O per hectare
paddy_healthy.pesticide: No pesticide required — preventive IPM only
paddy_healthy.description: Paddy crop is healthy. Maintain proper water management, balanced fertilization, and continue routine pest and disease scouting in the field.

paddy_leaf_blast.fertilizer_quantity: 100 kg N, 50 kg P2O5, 50 kg K2O per hectare
paddy_leaf_blast.pesticide_quantity: 0.6 g tricyclazole per litre, every 10–14 days
paddy_leaf_blast.description: Leaf blast causes diamond-shaped lesions. Use resistant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen, maintain field drainage, and spray tricyclazole at early infection.

potato_early_blight.fertilizer_quantity: 180 kg N, 100 kg P2O5, 120 kg K2O per hectare
potato_early_blight.pesticide_quantity: 2.5 g mancozeb per litre, every 10–14 days
potato_early_blight.description: Early blight causes dark concentric spots on lower leaves. Maintain adequate nitrogen and potash, hill properly, and apply protectant fungicide at 10–14 day intervals.

potato_healthy.fertilizer_quantity: 180 kg N, 100 kg P2O5, 120 kg K2O per hectare
potato_healthy.pesticide: No pesticide required — preventive care only
potato_healthy.description: Potato crop is healthy. Continue balanced fertilization, regular irrigation, and routine inspection for any early signs of late blight or insect attack.

potato_late_blight.fertilizer: NPK 15-15-15 with extra potassium and calcium
potato_late_blight.fertilizer_quantity: 180 kg N, 100 kg P2O5, 150 kg K2O per hectare
potato_late_blight.pesticide_quantity: 2.5 g metalaxyl-mancozeb per litre, every 7–10 days
potato_late_blight.description: Late blight is devastating in cool, wet weather. Use certified disease-free seed, destroy cull piles, and apply systemic fungicide at first sign of infection.

soybean_caterpillar.fertilizer_quantity: 25 kg N, 60 kg P2O5, 40 kg K2O per hectare
soybean_caterpillar.pesticide: Emamectin benzoate (5% SG) or Bt biopesticide
soybean_caterpillar.pesticide_quantity: 0.4 g emamectin per litre, every 10 days
soybean_caterpillar.description: Caterpillars defoliate soybean leaves. Install pheromone traps, spray Bt or emamectin benzoate at economic threshold level, and conserve natural enemies.

soybean_diabrotica_speciosa.fertilizer_quantity: 25 kg N, 60 kg P2O5, 40 kg K2O per hectare
soybean_diabrotica_speciosa.pesticide_quantity: 0.5 ml imidacloprid per litre, spray at ETL
soybean_diabrotica_speciosa.description: Diabrotica beetles feed on soybean leaves. Use seed treatment with imidacloprid, rotate with non-host crops, and apply foliar spray if beetle count exceeds threshold.

soybean_healthy.fertilizer_quantity: 25 kg N, 60 kg P2O5, 40 kg K2O per hectare
soybean_healthy.pesticide: No pesticide required — preventive care only
soybean_healthy.description: Soybean crop is healthy. Maintain rhizobium nodulation, balanced nutrition, and monitor regularly for any pest or disease pressure in the field.

tomato_bacterial_spot.fertilizer: NPK 15-15-15 with extra potassium and calcium
tomato_bacterial_spot.fertilizer_quantity: 120 kg N, 80 kg P2O5, 100 kg K2O per hectare
tomato_bacterial_spot.pesticide_quantity: 2 g copper + 0.5 g streptocycline per 10 litres water
tomato_bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial spot spreads in warm, wet conditions. Use certified disease-free seed, avoid overhead irrigation, and apply copper-based bactericide at first symptoms.

tomato_early_blight.fertilizer_quantity: 120 kg N, 80 kg P2O5, 100 kg K2O per hectare
tomato_early_blight.pesticide_quantity: 2.5 g mancozeb per litre, every 10–14 days
tomato_early_blight.description: Early blight causes dark concentric rings on lower leaves. Mulch the soil, stake plants, prune lower leaves, and apply protectant fungicide at 10–14 day intervals.

tomato_healthy.fertilizer_quantity: 120 kg N, 80 kg P2O5, 100 kg K2O per hectare
tomato_healthy.pesticide: No pesticide required — preventive neem oil only
tomato_healthy.pesticide_quantity: 5 ml neem oil per litre, bi-weekly
tomato_healthy.description: Tomato plant is healthy. Continue balanced fertilization with calcium for fruit quality, regular staking, and routine inspection for any pest or disease.

tomato_late_blight.fertilizer: NPK 15-15-15 with extra potassium and calcium
tomato_late_blight.fertilizer_quantity: 120 kg N, 80 kg P2O5, 120 kg K2O per hectare
tomato_late_blight.pesticide_quantity: 2.5 g metalaxyl-mancozeb per litre, every 7–10 days
tomato_late_blight.description: Late blight is a serious tomato disease. Destroy infected plants, avoid overhead irrigation, improve airflow, and spray systemic fungicide at first sign of disease.

wheat_healthy.fertilizer_quantity: 120 kg N, 60 kg P2O5, 40 kg K2O per hectare
wheat_healthy.pesticide: No pesticide required — preventive IPM only
wheat_healthy.description: Wheat crop is healthy. Continue timely irrigation at critical stages, balanced nitrogen application, and routine monitoring for rust or aphid attack.

wheat_mildew.fertilizer: NPK 15-15-15 with reduced nitrogen and extra potash
wheat_mildew.fertilizer_quantity: 100 kg N, 60 kg P2O5, 60 kg K2O per hectare
wheat_mildew.pesticide_quantity: 3 g sulphur per litre, every 10–14 days
wheat_mildew.description: Powdery mildew appears as white powdery patches. Avoid excess nitrogen, use resistant varieties, and spray sulphur or propiconazole at first sign of disease.

wheat_septoria.fertilizer_quantity: 120 kg N, 60 kg P2O5, 60 kg K2O per hectare
wheat_septoria.pesticide_quantity: 1 ml propiconazole per litre, every 14 days
wheat_septoria.description: Septoria causes small brown spots with yellow halos. Bury crop residue, rotate crops, and apply foliar fungicide at early flowering for best control.

wheat_yellowrust.fertilizer_quantity: 120 kg N, 60 kg P2O5, 60 kg K2O per hectare
wheat_yellowrust.pesticide_quantity: 1 ml propiconazole per litre, every 14 days
wheat_yellowrust.description: Yellow rust appears as yellow stripes on leaves. Plant resistant varieties, monitor at tillering stage, and spray triazole fungicide at first appearance of pustules.
